{{Nihongo|'''Kensō Soai'''|硤合 憲三|Soai Kensō| born 3 May 1950}}<ref name="a580">{{cite web |last=Pluta |first=Werner |title=Chemienobelpreis für die Entdeckung nichtlinearer Effekte |website=heise online |date=7 October 2026 |url=https://www.heise.de/news/Chemienobelpreis-fuer-die-Entdeckung-nichtlinearer-Effekte-11479206.html |language=de |access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref> is a Japanese [[organic chemist]], Professor Emeritus in the Department of Applied Chemistry at [[Tokyo University of Science]].

In 2026, he was  jointly awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]]  with [[Henri B. Kagan]]  "for the discovery of non-linear effects and [[autocatalysis]] in [[asymmetric synthesis|asymmetric organic synthesis]]."

==Biography==
Soai studied at the [[University of Tokyo]], where he received his Ph.D. in 1979 in [[organic synthesis]] under [[Teruaki Mukaiyama]] and was a fellow of the [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]]. He conducted his postdoctoral studies with [[Ernest L. Eliel]] at the [[University of North Carolina]]. In 1981, he became a lecturer at Tokyo University of Science, and was promoted to associate professor (1986) and full professor (1991).<ref name="s254" /> In 2026, he was  jointly awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]]  with [[Henri B. Kagan]]  "for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis."
<ref name=Nobel>{{Cite web |title=Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026 |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026/press-release/ |access-date=7 October 2026 |website=NobelPrize.org |language=en-US}}</ref> 

He is involved in asymmetric and [[enantioselective synthesis]], asymmetric [[autocatalysis]], and the origin of [[chirality (chemistry)|chirality]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/news/explainer-what-are-autocatalysis-and-non-linear-effects-and-why-have-they-won-the-2026-nobel-prize-in-chemistry/4024328.article|title=Explainer: what are autocatalysis and non-linear effects and why have they won the 2026 Nobel prize in chemistry?|first=Jamie|last=Durrani|work=Chemistry World|date=7 October 2026}}</ref> In 1995, Soai discovered a reaction with the chiral compound [[5-pyrimidyl alkanol]] that produced almost exclusively one of the two mirror-image forms of a molecule as a product, mimicking a process found in living organisms.<ref name="Nature1"/> In 2003, he was able to demonstrate this reaction with nonchiral reactants.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/10/07/2026-nobel-prize-in-chemistry-goes-to-france-s-henri-kagan-and-japan-s-kenso-soai_6758349_4.html|title=2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry goes to France's Henri Kagan and Japan's Kenso Soai|work=Le Monde|date=7 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2026/oct/07/nobel-prize-chemistry-awarded-work-on-mirror-image-molecules|title=Nobel prize in chemistry awarded for work on mirror-image molecules|date=7 October 2026|first=Linda|last=Geddes|work=The Guardian}}</ref><ref name="JT1"/> Specifically, the [[Soai reaction]] for alkylation of [[5-pyrimidyl alkanol|pyrimidine-5-carbaldehyde]] with [[diisopropylzinc]] is named after him. In this reaction, both reactants, which are non-chiral, produce the chiral product pyrimidyl alcohol, which further induces that same chirality in subsequent catalytic cycles.<ref name="p302">{{cite journal | last1=Athavale | first1=Soumitra V. | last2=Simon | first2=Adam | last3=Houk | first3=Kendall N. | last4=Denmark | first4=Scott E. | title=Demystifying the asymmetry-amplifying, autocatalytic behaviour of the Soai reaction through structural, mechanistic and computational studies | journal=Nature Chemistry | volume=12 | issue=4 | date=2020 | issn=1755-4330 | pmid=32203445 | pmc=7117993 | doi=10.1038/s41557-020-0421-8 | pages=412–423 | bibcode=2020NatCh..12..412A }}</ref><ref name="k376">{{cite journal | last=Soai | first=Kenso | title=The Soai reaction and its implications with the life's characteristic features of self-replication and homochirality | journal=Tetrahedron | volume=124 | date=2022 | doi=10.1016/j.tet.2022.133017 | article-number=133017 | url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0040402022004677 | access-date=7 October 2026}}</ref><ref name="n446">{{cite book | title=The soai reaction and related topic | publisher=Edizioni Artestampa | publication-place=Modena | date=2012 | isbn=978-88-6462-130-2 | page=}}</ref><ref name="Nature1">{{cite journal |last1=Gibney |first1=Elizabeth |last2=Naddaf |first2=Miryam |last3=Pichon |first3=Anne |last4=Castelvecchi |first4=Davide |last5=Callaway |first5=Ewen |title=Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of how 'handed' organic molecules can emerge |journal=Nature |date=7 October 2026 |volume=658 |issue=8136 |pages=589–590 |doi=10.1038/d41586-026-03093-0 |pmid=42844442 |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03093-0 |access-date=10 October 2026|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Soai was a visiting professor at several universities such as the [[ESPCI Paris]] (2001), [[Kyushu University]] (2005), [[Waseda University]] (2007–2010), [[University of Strasbourg]] (2008), and [[Jilin University]] (2010–2015).<ref name="s254" /> He retired as a professor in 2016.<ref name="JT1">{{cite news |last1=Otake |first1=Tomoko |title=Nobel winner Kenso Soai says he understood the significance of his research |url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/10/08/japan/science-health/kenso-soai-research-significance/ |access-date=10 October 2026 |work=Japan Times}}</ref>

* [[The Ryoji Noyori Prize|Ryoji Noyori Prize]] (2023)<ref>{{Cite web|title=高砂香料国際賞「野依賞」|url=https://www.ssocj.jp/award/noyori/|website=公益社団法人 有機合成化学協会|access-date=2026-10-07|language=ja}}</ref>
* [[Japan Academy Prize (academics)|Japan Academy Prize]] (2025)<ref name="f758">{{cite web | title=Japanischer Chemiker Kenso Soai erhält Nobelpreis für Chemie | website=Sumikai | date=7 October 2026 | url=https://sumikai.com/nachrichten-aus-japan/japanischer-chemiker-kenso-soai-erhaelt-nobelpreis-fuer-chemie-381377/ | language=de | access-date=8 October 2026}}</ref>
* [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]] (2026)<ref name=Nobel/>
* [[Order of Culture]] (2026)<ref>{{Cite web |url= https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOUD229PH0S6A021C2000000/|script-title=ja:文化勲章・功労者の業績と略歴 2026年度|access-date= October 23, 2026|date= October 23, 2026|website= The Nikkei|language=ja}}</ref>

In its 2026 Nobel announcement, the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences highlighted Soai's progression from his 1995 work on asymmetric autocatalysis to a 2003 reaction producing one of two possible mirror-image forms. It placed these results in the study of [[homochirality]] and the design of pharmaceutical synthesis. The prize money was shared equally with Henri B. Kagan.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026 – Press release |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026/press-release/ |website=NobelPrize.org |date=7 October 2026 |access-date=10 October 2026}}</ref>
